idiom_name: readonly record struct Interval<T>(T Lo, T Hi, BoundKind LoKind, BoundKind HiKind)
implementation_notes: C# ships no interval value: System.Range is index arithmetic for slicing (Start is an inclusive Index, End an exclusive Index, GetOffsetAndLength resolves them against a collection length) and cannot answer containment or overlap over a date or numeric domain. The idiom is therefore a readonly record struct over IComparable<T> carrying both endpoints and their BoundKind, with named factories (Closed, ClosedOpen, AtLeast, AtMost) and Contains/Overlaps/Intersect methods; record value equality, deconstruction and with-expressions come free, and the factory is the one place that validates End against Start.
pitfalls: default(Interval<T>) is a silently unset value: a null T with BoundKind.Closed, which record equality will happily compare as equal to another default instance - validate in the factory and consider a class when 'unset' must be distinguishable.

System.Range looks like the right type and is not: 0..2 on an array couples an inclusive start to an exclusive end and needs a collection length, so it cannot express [a, b] over dates or an unbounded side.

Nullable<T> endpoints need a generic constraint that Nullable<T> cannot satisfy directly (where T : struct), so open ends are usually expressed as a BoundKind enum plus a nullable field - keep the two in sync or the four cases stop being exhaustive.
IComparable<T> is not required to be a total order consistent with equality; for a custom domain type that breaks the contract, interval equality and Contains disagree.

variants.name: Noda Time Interval / DateInterval (time domain)
variants.implementation_notes: For the time domain Noda Time provides the value directly: Interval stores a start (inclusive) and an end (exclusive) instant, HasStart/HasEnd report whether a side is unbounded (a null endpoint is documented as stretching to the start or end of time) and Contains answers membership; DateInterval is the calendar-date counterpart and IYearMonthDay* types cover month-based periods. It fixes the bound kinds, so a model that needs closed ends converts deliberately at the edges instead of redefining the type.
pitfalls: Interval is documented as start-inclusive and end-exclusive, so a closed business period ("1st to 31st") must be converted on purpose or the final instant is silently excluded.
Start and End throw InvalidOperationException on an unbounded side; test HasStart/HasEnd first (the property returns bool rather than defaulting to a sentinel).

Equality is component-wise and ordering between intervals is not defined, so sorting a list of intervals requires comparing Start or Duration explicitly - and Noda Time values must not be mixed with System.DateTime in the same domain model.
